items.heading: Most Stay Most Stay Most
items.text: Most Stay Most Stay Most Stay Most stay-or-return decisions get made on a single loud factor, usually salary or a single family opinion, while four other real factors sit quietly in the background and surface later as regret or friction. The five-factor framework below puts all of them on the table together.

items.heading: Visa and Immigration Uncertainty Visa
items.text: Visa and Immigration Uncertainty Visa and immigration uncertainty is often the single biggest wildcard for people planning to stay, since lottery-based work visas and long green card backlogs put real control outside your hands.

items.heading: This Is the Factor People
items.text: This is the factor people most often underweight early and most often regret underweighting later. Staying abroad usually means staying inside someone else's timeline: a lottery result, a sponsorship policy, or a government-set processing backlog, not a decision fully in your own hands.

items.heading: There Is No Universally Correct
items.text: There is no universally correct answer. Career path, visa runway, family circumstances, and life stage need to be weighed together, not treated as one factor overriding the rest.

items.heading: Reported Survey Data Suggests Most
items.text: Reported survey data suggests most Indian students who study abroad still expect to build their career in India eventually, even if that intention shifts once real offers and visa outcomes appear.

items.heading: The "Coming Home" Adjustment
items.text: The "coming home" adjustment is a real, often underestimated cost that deserves as much planning as the decision to stay.
